title: Naming-error corrections from the 360 audit (Ware, Latvian, Maróczy diacritic, Réti alias)
description: Audit P0 micro-lot (docs/ocn-360-audit.md). Resolves the two verified wrong-name duplicates — 'Meadow Hay Trap' stays only on A.War.e5.Ra3 (1.a4 e5 2.Ra3 per Lichess) and 'Greco Variation' stays only on C.LtO.Nxe5.Qe7 (3.Nxe5 Qe7 per Lichess; Wikipedia confirms 3...Qf6 is the main line, so the Qf6 subtree is renamed to a Main Line stem, also killing the duplicated 'Latvian Greco Nc4, fxe4') — fixes the B.Sic.OKe.c4 'Maroczy' diacritic against its own attribution, and adds the missing 'Zukertort Opening' alias to A.Ret. canonical_name/aliases strings only; slugs frozen.

source_refs: Lot 3 evidence record (docs/lot-3-eco-a-eponyms-dry-run.md): the bare 1.Nf3 is catalogued separately as the Zukertort Opening; Wikipedia 'Réti Opening' notes Tartakower's 'Réti–Zukertort Opening'. The standard alternative name was missing from aliases.

external/lichess-openings TSV (CC0): 'Ware Opening: Meadow Hay Trap' = 1.a4 e5 2.Ra3; 'Ware Opening: Ware Gambit' = 1.a4 e5 2.a5 d5 3.e3 f5 4.a6; 'Latvian Gambit: Greco Variation' = 3.Nxe5 Qe7; the 3.Nxe5 Qf6 complex carries the Accepted sub-line names (Bilguer/Bronstein/Foltys/Leonhardt).

Wikipedia 'Latvian Gambit' (re-verified 2026-06-11): 3.Nxe5 Qf6 is 'considered the main line'; 'Greco Countergambit' is the historical name of the whole opening, and neither queen move is individually 'Greco' there.
